scenes.headline: How a top lab runs its kernels off NVIDIA
scenes.sub: DeepGEMM-Ascend and DeepEP-Ascend on Huawei's NPU
scenes.say: Hi there! One lab put its fastest kernels out in the open, running on a new kind of chip, not the usual one.

scenes.text: Serving a giant mixture of experts needs two kernels: one to do the matrix math, one to shuttle each token to its experts and back.
scenes.say: Serving a giant mixture of experts needs two kernels. One does the matrix math. The other shuttles each token to its experts and back.

left.title: The math
left.say: The first kernel is the matrix multiply. Attention and the experts are all big multiplies. This is where the compute goes.

right.title: The traffic
right.say: But the experts live on different chips. Every token travels out to them, and the answers travel back. That traffic is the second kernel.

scenes.title: The expert layer, fused into one pass

steps.say: A router sends each token to its chosen experts, scattered across the chips. That is dispatch.
Each expert multiplies the token, gates it, and multiplies again. Two matrix multiplies with an activation between.
The second multiply projects it back down. A shared expert runs locally all the while.
Combine gathers the results back home. All of it is one kernel, so nothing leaves on-chip memory.

items.say: There is no CUDA here. The kernel moves tiles by hand into fast on-chip buffers.
It feeds them to the matrix engine and keeps the pipeline full, so the engine never waits.
Results build up, then spill out at the end. That hand-written pipeline gets it near the limit.

scenes.title: Share of the chip's compute limit
scenes.say: The dense multiply reaches ninety nine point eight percent of the ceiling. The fused expert layer reaches ninety eight, lower, because it carries the traffic.

scenes.text: Two numbers, two ops. The ninety-eight is the harder win: a whole expert layer, communication included, kept near the limit.

recap: Two kernels: the math and the traffic
Ported to a new chip's matrix engine
Dense multiply near the limit, fused layer close behind
scenes.say: To recap: a math kernel and a traffic kernel, on a new chip, both near its limit.
